title: What If You Lived on a Planet 10 Times Heavier Than Earth?

scenes.text: What if you lived on a planet ten times heavier than Earth? You could never leave.
Scientists modeled a world 70 percent wider than Earth, like Kepler-20b, about 950 light years away.
To escape its gravity, you'd need about 2.4 times Earth's escape velocity.
That sounds small, but rockets need exponentially more fuel for every bit of extra speed.
An Apollo style moon mission would need a rocket of around 440,000 tonnes, mostly fuel.
Even launching a space telescope the size of Webb would take about 55,000 tonnes of fuel.
Chemical rockets might not be enough. Space travel could stay out of reach on a heavy world.
